title: StockPaperSim — Persona Paper-Trading Competition (Replay + Live Book)
description: One-year paper-trading competition between return-seeking strategy personas, with a real venue model (depth, spreads, market making, dated tick sizes and fees), a full audit trail and a dependency-free static site, and no live feed anywhere: the consolidated tape is not reachable, Yahoo's quote endpoint needs a crumb, Stooq refused the connection, and no bulk daily OHLCV for all 17 names was retrievable, so six live-data adapters (Alpaca, Polygon, Finnhub, Tiingo, Yahoo, Stooq) ship as the path to a genuinely real-time season but could not be exercised. Three runs are documented and re-read at the sixth pass (2026-09-22): Season 1 with 20 personas replaying the real S&P 500 and VIX path, republished with its numbers re-derived rather than patched; the legacy Live Book with 19 personas trading forward from official free series; and Season 2 with 19 personas in a reproducible research replay on collected daily bars, its roster having grown from 14 to 19 with three new slate personas (NFL, NBA, NCAA) and two forward-only probes while the complete ESPN NBA scoreboard (1,330 rows, 2025-10-21 to 2026-06-14) lets the NBA slate persona trade the full 2025-26 season. The sixth pass added real SEC Form 4 insider data: a rendered-extraction campaign plus an EDGAR full-text purchase locator now hold 86 filings and 216 parsed transactions across all ten tracked tickers (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, JPM, XOM, JNJ, PG, TSLA, MU, T), every filing dated on or after 2026-06-01, captured as the SEC's own XSL-rendered Form 4 views plus filing indexes into data/real/sec_agent/ with SHA-256 digests re-verified at staging; sim/edgar_rendered.py parses them fail-closed and scripts/stage_sec_rendered.py integrates the lane into the same JSONL the walk and bulk sets feed, de-duplicated on (accession, date, ticker, code, shares, price). Eleven filings parse to no Table I trade rows because they are derivative-only grants or balance-only rows and are flagged rather than dropped. The locator found eight code-P purchase filings and all eight are captured, so the buy-side insider signals are no longer NO-OBSERVATIONS; only one purchase in the window is by a CEO (TSLA, 2025-09-15, 25 lots / 2.57m shares) and one MSFT row is a broker-initiated purchase the officer disavowed and still counts because the rules are code tests. The quarterly structured bulk sets remain refused to the collection runner (HTTP 403 / rate gate, L-27), so this is a complementary rendered lane, not a replacement. Two real findings from this pass: a look-ahead bug that dated purchases by trade date rather than filing date (a two-business-day look-ahead normally, seven months for one late filing), fixed and pinned by tests, and two cluster personas that declared an exit they never coded and held TSLA for a year, also fixed. Season 2 now reports @InsiderCopycat_Max +12.0% and @CEO_CFO_Conviction +7.5%. The independent audits were executed here: scripts/independent_audit_season2.py reports TOTAL 5,513 checks · 5,513 passed · 0 failed plus a custody note of 327 files byte-identical, and scripts/independent_audit.py reports 763 and 611 checks passed with 0 failed on the season1 and season2 rehearsal manifests (1,374 in total). The test suite reports 697 green. The committed registers hold 86 irregularities (IR-01 to IR-86: 21 low, 41 medium, 24 high), 44 limitations and 55 items of remaining work. The project states plainly that the executable bars are collected Yahoo Finance files marked SECONDARY, that two of seventeen price series in Season 1 are real observations while the other fifteen are labelled simulations, and that the committed-price run is not eligible as an official-price competition.

Its insider signal is ready but has nothing to trade on. The extracted Form 4 window contains zero code-P open-market purchases, so @InsiderCluster_Live reports READY-NO-OBSERVATIONS and the insider participants hold no positions and say why, rather than substituting an aggregator for a filing or showing an empty result as a neutral one. Two MU filings were excluded for exceeding the page-fetch size budget, and 11 of the 65 parse to no Table I trade rows — all flagged, none dropped silently.

Data provenance is labelled rather than smoothed: the executable bars are collected Yahoo Finance files marked SECONDARY, only two of seventeen Season 1 price series are real observations with the other fifteen labelled simulations, and the committed-price run is explicitly not eligible as an official-price competition. The SEC quarterly structured bulk sets are still refused to its runner (HTTP 403 / rate gate, L-27).

Fast-moving repository: a single-commit README-only placeholder in the 2026-09-17 audit, it needed description rewrites in each audit since — the Season 2 roster went 14 to 19 personas (IRR-37), then the fourth pass landed the SEC Form 4 agent lane and moved tests 634 to 648, audit checks 1,870 to 1,871 and LIMITATIONS.json 43 to 44 (IRR-61).
